Kuntaka(la)
Rājānaka. Criticised strongly by his younger contemporary Mahimabhaṭṭa in Vyaktiviveka. Regarding Abhinavagupta, (

-1000 A. D.), his elder contemporary an. Kuntaka, see A. Sankaran, Theories of Rasa an. Dhvani, Uni. of Madras p.. 119-20; V. Raghavan, JOR. Madras VI. p.. 218-22 an. Ind. Cult. III. p.. 756-9. On various concepts an. K. an. Bhoja, see V. Raghavan, Bhoja's Śṛṅgāra Prakāśa, (1963), p.. 82-5, 87-9, 95-102, 117, 119-24, 318, 320, 339-46, 824-5.

Kuntaladevīkathā

Kuntaleśa
King of Kuntala, (Pravarasena) to whom Setubandha is ascribed by Kṛṣṇa in Bharatacarita (lokeSvalaGkAramapUrvasetuM babandha kIrtyA saha kuntalezaH).

Kuntale(kunte)śvaradautya
a poem or some verses relating to the incident of poet Kālidāsa going a. ambassador from Vikramāditya to the Kuntala King. Q. by Rājaśekhara in Kāvyamīmāṁsā, Bhoja in Śṛ. Pra. an. Kṣemendra in Aucityavicāracarcā. For a full discussion on it, see V. Raghavan, Bhoja's Śṛṅgāra Prakāśu, (1963) p.. 778-84; B. C. Law Vol. II. p.. 191-7.

Kuntāpasūkta,_ku._adhyāya,_kuntādhyāya

-136; might have belonged to another recension of Ṛv. No padapāṭha for them has been handed down; but their sacrificial use borne out by Aitareya an. Kauṣītaki, the latter giving the name Kuntāpa, the former the names of its components. See also Āśval. śr. sū.

Kunda
Jain inscriptional poet. a. of the Sārnāth Skt. inscriptions of Kumāradevī, queen of Gāhaḍvāla Govindacandra, ed. in Epi. Ind. IX. p.. 319-28.

Kundakīrti
Jain. a pupil of Kundakunda. ref. to by Vibudha Śrīdhara in his Śrutāvatāra (Siddhāntasārādisaṅgraha p. 318), Māṇik. Dig. Jain.

Kundakunda
Jain; of the Mūla an. Drāviḍa Saṅghas; personal name Padmanandi, the name KK. probably after the place where he lived, which is said be Koṇḍakunda in South India; on other traditional names given to him-Elācārya, Gṛdhrapiccha, Vakragrīva-no reliable evidence is available. Said to be a. pupil of Bhadrabāhu, i. e., Bh. II. Regarding his date, Dig. Paṭṭāvalīs assign him to 1st Cent. A. D.; the school founded by him is mentioned in a. ins. of 797 A. D. Three of his works were written for a royal patron Śivakumāra whom K. B. Pathak identifies (Ind.

. (1885). p. 15) with the Kadamba King Śiva Mṛgeśa (5th Cent. A. D.) an. Chakravartti Nainar with the Pallava King Śivaskandavarman Sac. Bk.. of the Jainas III. p. xii. ff.); Pt. N. R. Premi assigned him to 3rd Cent. A. D. A. N. Upadhye supports the traditional date of 1st Cent. A. D. See Intro. to his edn. of Pravacanasāra, p.. x-xxiii, Rāyacandra Jaina Śāstramālā, Bombay, 1935.
See also Peters. II. p.. 80-6; IV. Index of a. s. p.. xix-xx; BP. p.. 91 ff; CPB. Intro. p.. v.-vii. South Ind. Ins. I. no. 152; Ind. Ant. XXIII. p. 126. N. Premi, Jaina Hitaiṣī X. p.. 378 ff. A. N. Upadhye, Intro. to his edn. of Pravacanasāra, loc. cit. Viśvatattvaprakaśa, Jīvarāja Jaina Granthamālā 16. Sholapur, 1964, p.. 31-2.
Tradition attributes 84 works called Prābhṛtas or Pāhuḍas to him; but only a few of these are available; all his works are in Pkt.
--Aṣṭaprābhṛtas or the eight Pāhuḍas: (1) Darśana prābhṛta or Daṁsaṇa- [Page194-b] pāhuḍa (36 gāthās) (2) Cāritra prābhṛta or Cāritta pāhuḍa (in 44 gāthās) (3) Sūtra prābhṛta or Sutta pāhuḍa (27 gāthās). (4) Bodh. prābhṛta or Bodh. pāhuḍa (62 gāthās) on Āyatana, Caitya, Prātimā etc. (5) Bhāva prābhṛta or Bhāva pāhuḍa (163 gāthās.) (6) Mokṣa prābhṛta or Mokkha pāhuḍa (106 gāthās) (7) Liṅga prābhṛta or Liṅga pāhuḍa (22 gāthās) (8) Śīla prābhṛta or Sīla pāhuḍa (40 gāthās).
W. Denecke doubts Kundakunda's authorship of these (Festgabe Jacobi, p.. 163 ff.); but they are traditionally ascribed to KK. Śrutasāgara has commented on the first six of these (Pt.. Māṇik. Dig. Jain
; first six with C. an. the other two with Skt. Chāyā), which are together referred to a. Ṣaṭprābhṛtas or Chappāhuḍas. See Peters. II. p.. 80-4; 158-161; Wint., HIL.

. On Aṣṭaprābhṛtas see also Leumann, ZDMG. XI. p.. 297-312, A. N. Upadhye, loc. cit. p.. xxxiv-xxxvii.
For titles of several of the other Pāhudas of KK., see fn. 1, p. xxv, Intro., A. N. Upadhye, loc. cit.
